report.incidentSummary: At market open on 2026-10-19 at 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC), stock order placement failed for approximately 22.5% of requests with high p95 latency (~2000-2400 ms) and HTTP 503 errors on order-service. While the reporter initially suspected an external broker outage similar to PIR-2008, upstream broker metrics remained healthy. The investigation confirmed that configuration change CHG-48221, applied on Friday 2026-10-16, had reduced order-service db.pool.max_connections by 80% from 100 to 20. Under Monday's market open burst (orders surging ~5.8x to 29,210/min), the 20-connection pool instantly saturated, driving connection acquisition wait times past the 1000 ms timeout and yielding 507 HTTP 503 errors until traffic subsided around 04:26 UTC.
report.rootCauseStatement: Configuration change CHG-48221 deployed on 2026-10-16T13:35:00Z reduced order-service's db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 to reduce idle connections. During the first subsequent market-open volume surge on Monday 2026-10-19 (03:45 UTC), the reduced connection pool was immediately saturated at 20/20 connections, causing connection acquisition wait times to spike to >1000 ms and triggering 507 HTTP 503 errors due to connection acquisition timeouts.

hypotheses.cause: Configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20, leading to immediate pool exhaustion and 1000 ms acquisition timeouts during Monday's market open burst.
hypotheses.rationale: CHG-48221 directly reduced max pool connections from 100 to 20 on Friday afternoon. During Monday market open, db_pool_in_use pegged exactly at 20.0, db_pool_wait_ms jumped from ~2.5 ms to >1000 ms, p95 latency jumped to ~2400 ms while p50 stayed normal, and 507 HTTP 503 errors were logged citing 'pool 20/20 in use, waited 1000ms'.

hypotheses.cause: Upstream Broker API degradation, rate limiting, or gateway outage caused order failures and high latency.
hypotheses.rationale: Broker-connector upstream latency p95 peaked at only 226.7 ms, rate limiting was negligible (≤2/min), error rate remained under 0.4%, and zero 5xx or timeout errors were logged by broker-connector. Upstream broker dependencies operated normally.

hypotheses.cause: Market-open order volume surge (~5.8x traffic spike) caused capacity saturation on order-service database connections independently of prior pool sizing.
hypotheses.rationale: The primary database instance showed steady connection counts (130-145) and negligible lock wait times (3.5-4.5 ms). The failure was strictly constrained to order-service's internal pool cap of 20 connections resulting from CHG-48221, rather than backend database capacity exhaustion.

facts.statement: On 2026-10-16T13:35:00.000Z, configuration change CHG-48221 changed order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20.
At 2026-10-19T03:45:00.000Z, order-service request_rate jumped from 131.3 req/s to 709.9 req/s and orders_per_min surged from 5,024 to 29,210.
order-service db_pool_in_use reached and pegged at 20.04 connections from 03:45 UTC to 04:25 UTC.
order-service connection acquisition wait time (db_pool_wait_ms) rose from ~2.5 ms baseline to over 1000 ms (peaking at 1151 ms) between 03:46 UTC and 04:25 UTC.
order-service recorded 507 HTTP 503 error logs between 03:45:08 UTC and 04:25:45 UTC stating 'order failed: timeout acquiring DB connection (pool 20/20 in use, waited 1000ms)'.
order-service error_rate rose to ~22.76% from 03:46 to 04:23 UTC while order_success_rate dropped to 67.77%-76.72%.
order-service latency_p95_ms spiked to 2428 ms at 03:46 UTC while latency_p50_ms remained under 120 ms throughout the entire window.
The primary relational database active_connections remained steady around 130-145 and db_lock_wait_ms remained normal around 3.5-4.5 ms throughout the incident window.
broker-connector upstream latency p95 for orders peaked at 226.7 ms, rate limited count was at most 2/min, error rate remained below 0.38%, and zero 5xx or timeout errors were logged.

inferences.statement: The market open on 2026-10-19 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC) was the first peak trading session following the reduction of db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 on Friday afternoon.
The order failures and latency spikes were not caused by upstream broker API degradation or rate limiting, contrary to the on-call SRE's initial suspicion.

Because p50 latency remained low (~80-100 ms) while p95 latency jumped to >2000 ms, the overall request latency surge was driven by requests timing out after waiting 1000 ms for database connection acquisition.
Database connection exhaustion was strictly client-side pool starvation within order-service rather than a primary database instance bottleneck or lock contention.

assumptions.statement: The previous db.pool.max_connections setting of 100 was sufficient to handle market-open surges without connection acquisition timeouts.

timeline.event: Change CHG-48221 is deployed, lowering order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20.
NSE/BSE market opens. order-service order volume surges ~5.8x to 29,210 orders/min (709.9 req/s).
order-service database connection pool reaches 20/20 in use; first HTTP 503 error logged due to connection acquisition timeout after waiting 1000 ms.
order-service error_rate surges to 22.76%, p95 latency jumps to 2428 ms, and db_pool_wait_ms exceeds 1000 ms.
On-call SRE reports INC-2910, suspecting upstream broker degradation based on past incident PIR-2008.
Market-open trading rush tapers; last DB pool acquisition timeout error is recorded.
order-service db_pool_in_use drops below 20; db_pool_wait_ms recovers to ~3 ms and error rate returns to baseline (<0.5%).

confidence.rationale: High confidence based on conclusive alignment between the configuration reduction timeline (CHG-48221), order-service metrics (pool usage saturated at exactly 20.0, wait time exceeding 1000 ms), and 507 application error logs detailing the exact failure mechanism, alongside negative evidence ruling out upstream broker issues and backend DB locks.

gaps.description: Historical connection pool utilization metrics from prior Monday market opens before CHG-48221 were not queried.
gaps.impact: Minimal; the exact pool saturation at 20/20 and 1000 ms acquisition timeouts provide definitive confirmation of the capacity ceiling.

recommendedActions.action: Revert CHG-48221 or reconfigure order-service db.pool.max_connections back to 100 (or size dynamically to handle peak market-open concurrency).
recommendedActions.rationale: The 20-connection ceiling is insufficient for peak market open concurrency (700+ req/s), causing pool starvation and 503 errors.
recommendedActions.verification: Check order-service configuration reflects db.pool.max_connections >= 100 and monitor db_pool_in_use during subsequent peak traffic.

recommendedActions.action: Add an alert for order-service db_pool_in_use reaching >= 85% capacity and db_pool_wait_ms exceeding 100 ms.
recommendedActions.rationale: Enables proactive warning of connection pool exhaustion before requests start timing out at the 1000 ms limit.

recommendedActions.rationale: The incident responder assumed broker failure due to similarity with PIR-2008, delaying root cause discovery.
